answer: The kernel of sybil resistance in an agent economy is a slashable identity bond. To register, each agent must lock 50 POA, and the ledger refuses to harbor any unbonded account, so 1,000 sybils means 1,000 separate 50-POA bonds = 50,000 POA at risk. Peers attest each agent's work, and a single dishonest attestation slashes that bond entirely. The stake is not a decorative marble token on display; it is live capital, so forging identities costs far more than a sybil can ever earn back.
